title: How do we multiply 3874 by 101 in one line?
description: A number times one hundred one is the number with two zeros plus the number once more. The two rows are added from the right with carries, and the answer is checked by taking the number away again. Keeko doubts that writing the number twice is enough.
teaching_notes: One idea: times one hundred one is the number times one hundred plus the number, so the number is added to itself shifted two places. Watch for students who write the number twice side by side, which shifts it four places.

video_script.why: The child has met times eleven as ten times the number plus the number. Here the same idea works for one hundred one.
video_script.substitution: Split one hundred one as one hundred plus one, add the two rows from the right with carries, and check by taking the number away.
video_script.anchor: three thousand eight hundred seventy four times one hundred one
video_script.wrong_answer: write the number twice side by side
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko writes the number twice side by side. That shifts it four places, so it is times ten thousand one, which is far bigger than the answer.
video_script.payoff_line: Add the number to itself, shifted two places

final_answer.spoken: three hundred ninety one thousand two hundred seventy four

never_show: the number written twice, marked as right
maths_rules: the last two digits are 7 and 4, copied down
video_script.design: One idea: times one hundred one is the number with two zeros plus the number. Uses the method of the times eleven video. Wrong idea: write the number twice side by side. The two rows stay on the board through the doubt.
